## Purpose

This SOP describes the determination of five-day biochemical oxygen
demand (BOD~5~) in water and wastewater samples using the manometric
method (WTW OxiTop system). BOD~5~ is a measure of the dissolved
oxygen consumed by microorganisms during the aerobic decomposition of
organic matter over a five-day incubation period at 20 °C and serves
as a standard indicator of the organic pollution load in water.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Surface water, wastewater, and effluent samples
  analyzed for BOD~5~ using the WTW OxiTop manometric method in the
  EA Program laboratory
- **Does not apply to:** Carbonaceous BOD (CBOD) with nitrification
  inhibitor; BOD by Winkler titration or dissolved oxygen probe
  methods; chemical oxygen demand (COD)
- **Location:** Biogeochemistry Laboratory, Pomona College

## Definitions

- **Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD):** The mass of dissolved oxygen
  consumed per unit volume of sample by microbial oxidation of organic
  matter under aerobic conditions at 20 °C; expressed in mg/L.
- **BOD~5~:** BOD measured over a 5-day incubation period at 20 °C;
  the standard regulatory measure of organic pollution load in surface
  water and effluent.
- **Carbonaceous BOD (CBOD):** BOD attributable to carbon-containing
  organic compounds; measured in the presence of a nitrification
  inhibitor (allylthiourea) to prevent oxygen consumption by nitrifying
  bacteria from being included.
- **Dilution water:** Aerated, buffered, dechlorinated deionized water
  seeded with a bacterial inoculum; used to dilute concentrated samples
  to bring the expected BOD into the measurable range.
- **Manometric method (OxiTop):** A closed-system BOD measurement
  technique in which O~2~ consumption is tracked by measuring the
  resulting decrease in headspace pressure; CO~2~ is absorbed by NaOH
  pellets in the headspace.
- **Nitrification:** Microbial oxidation of ammonia to nitrate by
  nitrifying bacteria; consumes dissolved oxygen and can inflate BOD
  values if not inhibited in carbonaceous BOD analyses.
- **Seeding:** Addition of a microbial inoculum (e.g., diluted
  wastewater or settled sewage) to dilution water to ensure adequate
  microbial activity when samples lack native microorganisms.

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |

| Trained Personnel | Prepare reagents, run analyses, record results          |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Nutrient buffer solutions contain phosphate and
  ammonium salts; NaOH pellets (used as CO~2~ absorbent) are
  corrosive. Handle with gloves and avoid skin or eye contact.
- **Biological:** Wastewater samples may contain pathogens. Treat all
  samples as potentially infectious.
- **Physical:** Glass BOD bottles are fragile. Handle with care to
  avoid breakage.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses or goggles
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves

### Emergency Procedures

In case of chemical spill or exposure, refer to
[SOP-L004 Chemical Spill Response](SOP-L004-chemical-spill-response.qmd)
or call Campus Safety. For NaOH contact with skin or eyes, flush
immediately with copious water for at least 15 minutes and seek
medical attention.

### Equipment

| BOD~5~ incubation bottles (nominal 500 mL) | Brown glass, with bottle neck adapter |
| Rubber quivers (CO~2~ absorber holders) | One per bottle                          |
| Incubator set to 20.0 +/- 1.0 °C     | Verify temperature daily                 |
| Magnetic stirrer platform (in incubator) | Low-speed continuous stirring          |
| Magnetic stir bars                    | One per bottle                           |

| Micropipette, 100--1000 $\mu$L        | With disposable tips                     |
| pH meter                              | Calibrated per [SOP-L300](SOP-L300-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd) |
| Air pump with diffuser stone          | For aerating dilution water              |
| 1000 mL volumetric flask or beaker    | For dilution water preparation           |

### Consumables

| Item                          | Storage          | Notes                       |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------|:----------------------------|
| NaOH pellets                  | Desiccator       | CO~2~ absorbent; 2 pellets per bottle |
| Phosphate buffer solution     | Refrigerator     | See Section 6              |
| MgSO~4~ solution              | Shelf            | See Section 6              |
| CaCl~2~ solution              | Shelf            | See Section 6              |
| FeCl~3~ solution              | Shelf            | See Section 6              |
| Seed inoculum (if needed)     | Fresh            | Settled domestic wastewater or commercial seed |


## Reagents and Standards

### Dilution Water Nutrient Solutions

Prepare the following stock solutions. Add 1 mL of each per liter of
dilution water.

1. **Phosphate buffer:** Dissolve 8.5 g KH~2~PO~4~, 21.75 g
   K~2~HPO~4~, 33.4 g Na~2~HPO~4~·7H~2~O, and 1.7 g NH~4~Cl in
   approximately 500 mL deionized water and dilute to 1 L. The pH
   should be 7.2.
2. **Magnesium sulfate:** Dissolve 22.5 g MgSO~4~·7H~2~O in
   deionized water and dilute to 1 L.
3. **Calcium chloride:** Dissolve 27.5 g CaCl~2~ in deionized water
   and dilute to 1 L.
4. **Ferric chloride:** Dissolve 0.25 g FeCl~3~·6H~2~O in deionized
   water and dilute to 1 L.

### Dilution Water Preparation

1. Fill a clean 1 L vessel with deionized water.
2. Add 1 mL of each nutrient stock solution (Section 6.1).
3. Aerate the dilution water with the air pump for at least one hour
   to bring dissolved oxygen to near saturation.
4. Verify pH is between 6.8 and 7.2; adjust with dilute HCl or NaOH
   if necessary.
5. Allow the water to equilibrate to 20 °C before use.

### Measuring Range and Volume Selection

The volume of sample placed in the BOD bottle depends on the expected
BOD~5~ concentration. Use the table below to select the appropriate
sample volume. Each analysis requires one blank bottle (dilution water
only) and at least two replicate sample bottles.

| Expected BOD~5~ (mg/L) | Total volume in bottle (mL) | Sample volume (mL) | Dilution water volume (mL) |
|:------------------------|:----------------------------|:--------------------|:--------------------------|
| 0--40                   | 432                         | 216                 | 216                       |
| 0--80                   | 365                         | 182.5               | 182.5                     |
| 0--200                  | 250                         | 125                 | 125                       |
| 0--400                  | 164                         | 82                  | 82                        |
| 0--800                  | 97                          | 48.5                | 48.5                      |
| 0--2000                 | 43.5                        | 21.75               | 21.75                     |

: Volume selection for WTW OxiTop BOD~5~ analysis based on expected concentration. {#tbl-volumes}

For most surface water samples in the EA Program, the 0--200 mg/L
range (125 mL sample + 125 mL dilution water) is a reasonable starting
point. If the expected concentration is unknown, run samples at two
different dilutions.


## Procedure

### Preparation (Day 0)

1. Calibrate the pH meter per
   [SOP-L300](SOP-L300-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd).
2. Prepare dilution water as described in Section 6.2. Make enough for
   all bottles (blanks and samples). For a standard run with one blank
   and two sample bottles at the 0--200 range, prepare at least 800 mL.
3. Collect or thaw samples. If samples have been refrigerated, allow
   them to equilibrate to 20 °C. If samples require seeding, add a
   known volume of seed inoculum to both sample and blank bottles.
4. Verify that all OxiTop manometers are functional (battery check,
   reset previous readings).

### Bottle Setup

1. Place a clean magnetic stir bar in each BOD~5~ incubation bottle.
2. Using the graduated cylinder, measure the appropriate volume of
   sample into each sample bottle (see @tbl-volumes).
3. Add the corresponding volume of dilution water to each sample
   bottle.
4. For the blank bottle, add dilution water only (total volume should
   match the sample bottles).
5. Place 2 NaOH pellets in each rubber quiver.
6. Insert the quiver into the neck of each bottle. The quiver must sit
   above the liquid surface; the NaOH absorbs CO~2~ produced during
   microbial respiration, ensuring that the pressure drop measured by
   the manometer reflects only oxygen consumption.
7. Screw the OxiTop manometer head onto each bottle. Ensure a
   gas-tight seal.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Label each bottle clearly (Blank, Sample A-1, Sample A-2, etc.) on
both the bottle and the manometer. Record the bottle assignments in
your lab notebook before starting incubation.
:::

### Incubation

1. Place all bottles on the magnetic stirrer platform inside the
   incubator set to 20.0 +/- 1.0 °C.
2. Activate the OxiTop manometers to begin recording pressure.
3. Incubate for five days (120 +/- 2 hours) in the dark. The
   incubator door should remain closed except for brief checks.
4. Verify incubator temperature at least once daily and record in the
   instrument logbook.

### Reading Results (Day 5)

1. After five days, read the BOD~5~ value displayed on each OxiTop
   manometer. The instrument converts the measured pressure decrease
   to mg/L BOD~5~ automatically based on the selected measuring
   range.
2. Record all readings in the lab notebook, including: date and time
   of setup, date and time of reading, incubator temperature log,
   measuring range selected, sample identification, and
   replicate values.
3. Remove bottles from the incubator. Discard sample water per
   Section 9. Clean bottles and stir bars thoroughly with hot water
   and laboratory detergent; rinse with deionized water.


## Data Analysis and Calculations

### OxiTop Direct Reading

The OxiTop system calculates BOD~5~ internally from the pressure
decrease in the bottle headspace. The displayed value in mg/L already
accounts for the measuring range selected during setup. Record this
value directly.

### Blank Correction

Subtract the blank BOD~5~ reading from each sample reading:

$$
\text{BOD}_{5,\text{corrected}} = \text{BOD}_{5,\text{sample}} - \text{BOD}_{5,\text{blank}}
$$

The blank value should be less than 0.2 mg/L for unseeded dilution
water. If the blank exceeds 0.2 mg/L, investigate the dilution water
quality and consider re-running the analysis.

### Dilution Factor

If the sample was diluted beyond the standard OxiTop protocol (e.g.,
for highly concentrated wastewater), apply the appropriate dilution
factor:

$$
\text{BOD}_{5,\text{final}} = \text{BOD}_{5,\text{corrected}} \times \frac{V_{\text{total}}}{V_{\text{sample}}}
$$

For standard OxiTop runs where the measuring range was set correctly,
the dilution factor is already incorporated into the displayed result.


## Quality Control

- Run at least one blank per analytical batch.
- Run duplicate sample bottles for each sample; the relative percent
  difference (RPD) between duplicates should be less than 20%.
- If available, include a glucose-glutamic acid (GGA) standard check
  solution at a concentration of 300 mg/L combined (150 mg/L each).
  The expected BOD~5~ of the GGA standard is 198 +/- 30.5 mg/L
  (Standard Methods 5210 B).
- The blank BOD~5~ should be less than 0.2 mg/L (unseeded) or less
  than 0.6 mg/L (seeded).
- Verify incubator temperature is 20.0 +/- 1.0 °C throughout the
  incubation period.
- Log all QC results. If QC criteria are not met, flag the data and
  consult the PI before reporting.


## Troubleshooting

| Problem                              | Possible Cause                        | Corrective Action                     |
|:-------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|
| No pressure change after 5 days      | Dead battery in manometer; poor seal  | Check battery; reseat manometer       |
| Blank BOD~5~ too high                | Contaminated dilution water or glassware | Reclean bottles; prepare fresh dilution water |
| Replicate RPD exceeds 20%            | Heterogeneous sample; pipetting error | Mix samples well; check pipette calibration |
| BOD~5~ exceeds measuring range       | Sample more concentrated than expected | Re-run at a higher range (lower sample volume) |
| Negative BOD~5~ reading              | Leak in bottle seal; NaOH saturated   | Inspect seal; use fresh NaOH pellets  |


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Analyzed sample water         | Drain with copious water (if non-hazardous); collect if industrial wastewater |
| NaOH pellets (used)           | Dissolve in water, neutralize, drain     |
| Dilution water                | Drain                                    |
| Broken glass                  | Sharps container                         |

## Training Record

Before performing BOD~5~ analysis independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the WTW OxiTop operating manual
4. Observe a trained operator perform the complete procedure (setup
   through Day 5 reading)
5. Perform the analysis under supervision with acceptable QC results
   (duplicate RPD within 20%; blank within criteria)
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
